propositions.text: This is an appeal filed by XXXX XXXX against a May 16, 2016 RPD decision rejecting her refugee claim.
propositions.quote: This is an appeal filed by XXXX XXXX against a decision rendered on May 16, 2016, by the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), which rejected her refugee protection claim by determining that she was not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states this appeal challenges the RPD's May 16, 2016 decision rejecting the appellant's refugee claim under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The appellant asks the RAD to set aside the RPD determination, refer the matter for re-determination and give other directions.
propositions.quote: The appellant is asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to set aside the determination of the RPD, refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination and give any other directions that it considers appropriate.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant asks the RAD to set aside the RPD decision, refer the matter for re-determination, and give other directions.

propositions.text: The appellant did not present new evidence under subsection 110(4) IRPA and is not requesting a hearing under subsection 110(6) IRPA.
propositions.quote: The appellant did not present any new evidence under subsection 110(4) of the IRPA and is not requesting a hearing under subsection 110(6) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant did not present new evidence or request a hearing under IRPA subsections 110(4) or 110(6).

propositions.text: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.

propositions.text: Under subsection 111(1) IRPA, the RAD allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD determination and refers the matter to a differently constituted panel for re-determination.
propositions.quote: Under subsection 111(1) of the IRPA, the RAD allows the appeal, sets aside the determination of the RPD and refers the matter of XXXX XXXX to a differently constituted panel for re-determination of this refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD decision, and refers the matter for re-determination under IRPA 111(1).

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is allowed.

propositions.text: The appellant is a XXXX-year-old woman from Cameroon who was forced into a polygamous marriage at 17 and suffered violence and abuse.
propositions.quote: The appellant is a XXXX-year-old woman from Cameroon. She alleges that when she was 17, she was forced to become the second wife of a polygamous man (hereafter XXXX) in exchange for a dowry paid to her father. She was subjected to violence by her co-wife, her co-wife's brothers and her in-laws. Her husband was verbally abusive toward her and never intervened to protect her.

propositions.text: The appellant filed police complaints twice but received no help and could not seek divorce due to dowry repayment issues.
propositions.quote: The appellant filed a complaint with the police on two occasions, but they refused to help her. She could not seek a divorce because her family would not have been able to repay the dowry.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges forced polygamous marriage, abuse, police inaction, and inability to divorce due to dowry repayment.

propositions.text: After returning to Cameroon in 2015, the appellant was chased from home, learned of her children's suspicious deaths, and was threatened when seeking answers.
propositions.quote: The appellant alleges that when she returned to Cameroon in XXXX 2015 after a two-month trip to Canada with her husband, she was chased from the family home by her co-wife. She subsequently learned of the tragic death of her two children, whom she had entrusted to her co-wife before her trip to Canada. She was beaten and threatened several times by her co-wife's family when she tried to get answers about what had happened to her children, who had died under suspicious circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges being chased from home, children's suspicious deaths, and threats when seeking answers after returning to Cameroon in 2015.

propositions.text: The appellant left Cameroon on XXXX 28, 2016, came to Canada, and claimed refugee protection the day after arrival.
propositions.quote: The appellant left her country on XXXX 28, 2016, to come to Canada. She claimed refugee protection the day after she arrived.

propositions.text: The Minister intervened before the RPD.
propositions.quote: The Minister intervened before the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant left Cameroon in 2016, claimed refugee protection upon arrival in Canada, and the Minister intervened before the RPD.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the appellant's claim, finding her not credible and that she failed to establish marriage, polygamy, children, and domestic abuse.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected the appellant's refugee protection claim, finding that she was not credible. The RPD was of the opinion that the appellant failed to establish that she was married to XXXX, that it was a polygamous marriage, that she had children and that she had been subjected to domestic abuse.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim, finding the appellant not credible and failing to establish key facts.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred in evidence interpretation and credibility assessment, blaming husband for inaccuracies.
propositions.quote: The appellant argues that the RPD made several errors when interpreting the evidence and assessing her credibility. She claims that the inaccuracies concerning her children in her applications for a visa to travel to Canada and the United States of America were the fault of her husband, to whom she was subservient.

propositions.text: The appellant claims the RPD did not properly consider Guideline 4 on women refugee claimants fearing gender-related persecution.
propositions.quote: She states that the RPD did not really consider Guideline 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

propositions.text: The appellant submits errors on birth and death certificates about her child’s gender are unsurprising due to Cameroonian authorities.
propositions.quote: She submits that it is not surprising that Cameroonian authorities made an error on the birth certificate and the death certificate of one of her children, indicating that he was female rather than male.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the marriage certificate evidence is not contradictory and the RPD’s finding on domestic abuse is ambiguous.
propositions.quote: She argues that the evidence relating to the marriage certificate is not contradictory. She submits that the RPD's finding that she failed to establish that she was a victim of domestic abuse is ambiguous.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred in credibility, did not consider Guideline 4, and misinterpreted evidence on children, marriage, and abuse.

propositions.text: The RAD's role in appeals is defined by Federal Court of Appeal in Huruglica and by a three-member RAD panel in X(Re).
propositions.quote: The RAD's role in an appeal was defined by the Federal Court of Appeal in Minister of Citizenship and Immigration v. Huruglica1 and by the three-member RAD panel in X(Re), 2007 CanLII 33034 (CA IRB).2

paragraphs.summary: The RAD's role in appeals is defined by Huruglica and X(Re) decisions.

propositions.text: The RAD must conduct a reasoned, thorough, comprehensive, independent review and apply correctness standard to RPD findings.
propositions.quote: As established in Huruglica, supra, the RAD must conduct a reasoned, thorough, comprehensive and independent review of the evidence presented. The RAD must normally apply the standard of correctness to all RPD findings.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must independently review evidence and apply correctness standard to RPD findings.

propositions.text: For RPD credibility findings, RAD decides whether to defer based on RPD's advantageous position, explaining meaningful advantage if deferring.
propositions.quote: However, with regard to RPD findings based on the credibility of oral evidence, the RAD must determine, in each case, whether it owes deference to the RPD by determining whether the RPD truly benefited from an advantageous position. Where the RAD finds that deference is warranted, it is obligated to explain how the RPD enjoyed a meaningful advantage with respect to the credibility finding.

propositions.text: In some cases, RAD may assess credibility findings using a reasonableness standard modified for RAD context, per X(Re).
propositions.quote: In certain cases, the RAD may assess that finding using a standard of reasonableness, modified to apply to the RAD context, as per the decision in X(Re), 2007 CanLII 33034 (CA IRB).

paragraphs.summary: RAD must decide whether to defer to RPD credibility findings, explaining advantage; sometimes uses modified reasonableness standard.

propositions.text: The RAD will defer to RPD findings if RPD had meaningful advantage assessing testimony but will examine overall credibility under correctness standard.
propositions.quote: In this case, I will give deference to the RPD's findings if I determine that it enjoyed a meaningful advantage in assessing the appellant's testimony. Nevertheless, I will examine the overall credibility finding using the correctness standard.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will defer to RPD if it had meaningful advantage but will review overall credibility under correctness standard.

propositions.text: The issue is whether the RPD erred in assessing the appellant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The issue is whether the RPD erred when assessing the appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The issue is whether the RPD erred in assessing appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: After reviewing the hearing recording, file, memorandum, and evidence, the RPD's decision is wrong for reasons to follow.
propositions.quote: Having listened to the electronic recording of the hearing, read the entire file, considered the appellant's memorandum and conducted an independent assessment of the evidence, I conclude that the RPD's decision is wrong for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD decision is wrong after independent review and will explain reasons.

propositions.text: The court analyzed RPD findings and evidence considering Guideline 4 on women refugee claimants fearing gender-related persecution.
propositions.quote: I must specify that I analyzed the RPD's findings and assessed the evidence on the record in consideration of Guideline 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

propositions.text: Guideline 4 applies because appellant alleges forced polygamous marriage, subservience, abuse, and trauma from children's deaths.
propositions.quote: This guideline applies in this case because the appellant alleges that she was trapped in a forced marriage to a polygamous man, forced to follow her husband's orders, subjected to abuse within the family home and traumatized by the tragic and suspicious death of two of her three children.

paragraphs.summary: The court analyzed evidence considering Guideline 4 due to appellant's allegations of forced marriage, abuse, and trauma.

propositions.text: The court also considered appellant's allegations in light of documentary evidence on conditions in Cameroon in the NDP.
propositions.quote: I also considered the appellant's troubling allegations in light of the documentary evidence in the NDP regarding conditions in Cameroon.

paragraphs.summary: The court considered appellant's allegations alongside documentary evidence on Cameroon conditions in the NDP.

propositions.text: The issue of appellant's polygamous marriage to XXXX is determinative for the refugee claim based on fear of persecution by co-wife and family.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the issue of the appellant's polygamous marriage to XXXX is determinative because the refugee protection claim is based on her fear of being persecuted by her co-wife, her co-wife's family and her husband's brother.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the polygamous marriage issue determinative for the refugee claim based on fear of persecution.

propositions.text: Appellant says she did not fill US visa documents and just followed husband's orders; argues RPD would decide differently if Guideline 4 considered.
propositions.quote: Regarding the name of her husband, which is different in the two visa applications for the United States, the appellant submits that she did not fill out the documents for these visa applications and that she merely followed her husband's orders. She argues that that might be unbelievable to the RPD but that it would have reached a different conclusion if it really had considered Guideline 4.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues she did not fill US visa forms and RPD would decide differently if Guideline 4 applied.

propositions.text: Appellant submits she was subservient and uninformed, like many women in African societies, following husband's orders without understanding reasons.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits that she was cast aside and did not take part in decisions that concerned her, as she was given little information and was subservient to her husband, like women in many African societies, including Cameroon. She was no exception: she did what she was told, whether or not she understood the reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant says she was subservient and uninformed, following husband's orders as in many African societies.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellant did not establish marriage to XXXX or polygamous marriage due to contradictions in evidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD was of the opinion that the appellant did not establish that she was married to XXXX or that it was a polygamous marriage because of the numerous contradictions in the evidence presented.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant did not establish marriage or polygamy due to contradictory evidence.

propositions.text: RPD noted appellant's two US visa applications named different husbands and was unsatisfied with her explanation that husband completed forms and lied.
propositions.quote: The RPD considered the two visa applications for the United States filed in 2010 and 2015, in which the appellant states that her husband is XXXX, whereas she claims to be married to XXXX. The RPD was not satisfied with her explanation for this contradiction, that is, that it was her husband, XXXX, who had completed the steps for these two visa applications and that he had lied about certain facts, including her husband's name and the number of children she had, and she did not know why.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's explanation for contradictory husband names on visa applications unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: RPD did not believe appellant was in polygamous marriage due to contradictions in marriage certificate.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not believe that the appellant was in a polygamous marriage with XXXX because of contradictions that arose on reading the marriage certificate filed in evidence.

paragraphs.summary: RPD disbelieved appellant's polygamous marriage claim due to marriage certificate contradictions.

propositions.text: RPD noted appellant's deceased father named as witness on marriage certificate but found contradictory evidence on his death date and was unsatisfied with appellant's explanation.
propositions.quote: First, the RPD notes in its decision that the appellant's deceased father is named as a witness on the marriage certificate issued on XXXX XXXX, 2009, and that the evidence relating to his date of death is contradictory. The RPD was not satisfied with the appellant's answers.

propositions.text: Appellant testified father died in 2006; error in form stating 2010 was by helper; uncle with same name acted as witness.
propositions.quote: According to the appellant's testimony, her father died in 2006, and her answer in the IMM5669 form, that he died on XXXX XXXX, 2010, was an error made by the person who had helped her complete her forms. The appellant explained that it was an uncle who has the same name as her father who had acted as a witness at her wedding.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found contradictory evidence on father's death date; appellant explained form error and uncle as witness.
